checked: Required closure matches registration verifier source prefixes plus workflow, pyproject, publication/specification documents, four pinned public metadata records, randomization evidence and feature-readiness records.
No reused before/after snapshots: both are constructed by reading current source bytes during this invocation.
Actual commit before and after is separately captured; a changed commit, changed source or unsuccessful summary prevents recorder success.
Exact command, child identity, subprocess exit, complete combined log/hash and test count are recorded.
Output directory must not already exist; individual logs/JSON outputs use exclusive creation.
No source mutation, actual scientific capture, entropy or registration action is invoked.

closed_findings.R1: HEAD source paths are independently enumerated by git ls-tree; exact index/HEAD path equality is required and required closure derives from HEAD. Fresh working/index/committed-byte maps must match before subprocess execution.
closed_findings.R2: Exactly one parsed unittest count must be positive, the log must contain an exact OK line without skipped=, and actual child exit must be zero for recorder success.

limitations: This is review, not execution; it does not assert clean HEAD/index or any test success. Root must commit the reviewed closure before invoking it.
An exception/interruption after child execution may leave the exclusive log without a final execution receipt; such an incomplete run supplies no successful engineering receipt.
Source freeze assumes the cooperating project process; this is not a malicious-concurrent-writer sandbox or interpreter/OS attestation.
The registration verifier and exact-commit CI must independently check the eventual receipt and published source closure.
